items.claim: An unquoted service path containing spaces lets an attacker place a malicious executable at an earlier search location to gain SYSTEM privileges.
items.body: When a service binary path has spaces and no quotes, Windows resolves it ambiguously. For C:\Program Files\My App\service.exe it tries C:\Program.exe, then C:\Program Files\My.exe, then the real path. If the attacker can write to C:\ or an intermediate directory, placing a malicious binary at the first resolvable location causes it to run as SYSTEM when the service starts.
items.disproof: The service path is fully quoted, or no writable directory exists in the resolution chain.

sources.quote: If path is C:\\Program Files\\My App\\service.exe, Windows tries
An attacker that can write to the C:\\ directory would be able to place an executable file named Program.exe in the directory.

items.claim: Windows resolves DLLs in a fixed search order, so a writable directory earlier in the order can be abused to hijack a privileged process.
items.body: The standard DLL search order is: application directory, System32, System, Windows, current directory, then PATH directories. If an attacker can write to a directory that appears before the legitimate DLL location, placing a malicious DLL there causes it to load into a privileged process, yielding code execution as that process.
items.disproof: All directories in the search order are non-writable by the attacker, or DLL Safe Search / KnownDLLs prevents the hijack.

sources.quote: Windows searches for DLLs in a specific order.

items.claim: A privileged service loading a non-existent DLL from a writable PATH directory can be hijacked by placing a malicious DLL with the missing name.
items.body: Services like IKEEXT load wlbsctrl.dll which does not exist by default. If a writable directory is in the system or user PATH, the attacker places a malicious wlbsctrl.dll there. When the service starts or restarts, it loads the attacker DLL and executes it as SYSTEM.
items.disproof: The missing DLL is loaded from an absolute path or a non-writable directory, or the service does not run as SYSTEM.

sources.quote: Common vulnerable service: IKEEXT (IKE and AuthIP IPsec Keying Modules)
sources.locator: DLL Search Order Hijacking in Services

sources.quote: A low privileged user can place a malicious DLL file with the same name as the missing DLL in one of these directories.
